q: How many km per litre should a loaded Indian truck give by size, and how do I check a transporter's diesel claim?
title: Check a transporter's truck diesel claim
short: There is no single official km per litre for a loaded truck; it depends on gross weight, load, route, speed and driving. Check a claim by working out km per litre from full-tank fills and odometer readings, then comparing it with your own trips on the same lane in the same truck class.
audience: Logistics managers verifying freight emissions and fuel surcharges

ol: Fill the tank full at the start and note the odometer.
At the end, fill full again at the same pump if possible and note the odometer.
km per litre = km between fills / litres put in at the second fill.
Repeat over several trips. One trip can mislead because of traffic, ghats, loading delays or a half-full tank.

ul: Gross vehicle weight and load: a loaded trip uses more diesel than the empty return.
Route: hill sections, city stretches and bad roads cut km per litre.
Speed and idling: long waits at gates and tolls with the engine running burn diesel for zero km.
Vehicle: axle configuration, tyre pressure, engine age and whether it is BS IV or BS VI.

sections.h: Red flags in a diesel claim
ul: Litres billed that imply a much lower km per litre than your history for the same lane and class.
Distance that exceeds the e-way bill or GPS route by a wide margin.
Round-number litres on every trip, or fills with no pump receipt.
Identical claims for loaded and empty legs.

p: Litres x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre gives tank-to-wheel CO2. Divide by tonnes x km for kg CO2 per tonne-km. The default per tonne-km factors for India are well-to-wheel CO2e and include fuel production and typical empty running, so a tank-to-wheel figure from a fair claim should sit below the default for that truck class. A result well above it is worth questioning; a result below it does not prove the claim is right.

example.title: Worked example: a 1,450 km lane in a tractor-trailer carrying 25 t
lines: Transporter claims 580 litres: 1,450 / 580 = 2.5 km per litre
Your last ten trips on this lane in the same class averaged 3.4 km per litre (your records)
Expected litres: 1,450 / 3.4 = 426 litres, so the claim is 580 / 426 = 1.36, or 36 percent higher
CO2 at the claim: 580 x 2.68 = 1,554 kg; at your average: 426 x 2.68 = 1,142 kg
Per tonne-km at the claim: 1,554 / (25 x 1,450) = 0.043 kg CO2, below the 0.0551 kg CO2e well-to-wheel default for a tractor-trailer
example.note: The CO2 cross-check passes here, yet the claim is still 36 percent above your own history. Your lane history is the stronger test.

senseible: Senseible reads diesel invoices and fuel slips at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre, and a quantity that looks abnormal costs 25 points in its rule checks, so the line does not pass as Verified without review. Its logistics calculator gives per tonne-km figures by Indian truck class for comparison.
